hypothesis: SIC-C-c asks whether restricting to a specific inductive-bias hypothesis class can restore uniform polynomial-in-d_Z sample complexity for the continuous-case learnability problem of paper section 2.5b (Theorem 6). For the linear-ICA class --- latent Z with independent non-Gaussian marginals (Laplace(0, 1)), square orthogonal mixing matrix A, observation X = A * Z --- sklearn FastICA on N samples of X, evaluated by the Amari index amari(P) with P = W * A, is predicted to (a) achieve Amari <= 0.02 at N = 10000 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8}; (b) reach the polynomial-fit threshold Amari <= 0.03 with a smallest-N that grows only polynomially in d_Z (fitted log-log slope b <= 3.0); (c) yield a nonincreasing Amari(N) curve at every d_Z modulo a 0.01 numerical wobble; and (d) at d_Z = 8 land the linear-ICA sample complexity at least 20x below the Theorem 6 exponential bound ceil((D_Z / eps)^{d_Z} * ln((D_Z / eps)^{d_Z} / eps_rel)) with D_Z = 1, eps = 0.25, eps_rel = 0.05, c = 1.

gates.LICA_LINEAR_ICA_CONVERGES_AT_LARGEST_N: At N = 10000, the Amari index averaged over 8 trials is <= 0.02 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8}.
gates.LICA_SAMPLE_COMPLEXITY_POLYNOMIAL_IN_D_Z: For every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8} there is a smallest N in the sweep {200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000} with averaged Amari <= 0.03; the linear regression log(N_needed(d_Z)) = a + b * log(d_Z) has fitted slope b <= 3.0.
gates.LICA_AMARI_MONOTONE_IN_N_AT_EVERY_D_Z: For every d_Z, the averaged Amari curve is nonincreasing in N modulo a numerical tolerance of 0.01 (i.e. amari_mean at N_{i+1} <= amari_mean at N_i + 0.01).
gates.LICA_ESCAPES_THEOREM_6_EXPONENTIAL: At d_Z = 8, the linear-ICA N_needed to reach Amari <= 0.03 is at most 1/20 of the Theorem 6 exponential bound ceil(1 * (1/0.25)^{8} * ln((1/0.25)^{8} / 0.05)) = 923146; empirically N_needed(d_Z=8) = 2000, escape ratio 461.573x.

compute.sampling: Per (d_Z, trial) draw a Haar-orthogonal A via signed QR of a Gaussian and Laplace(0, 1) latents Z of size (max(N_VALUES), d_Z); every smaller N reuses the first N samples of the same draw as a prefix. sklearn FastICA(parallel, logcosh, whiten='unit-variance', max_iter=2000, tol=1e-6, random_state=trial).
